newsitem.title: USA: Avon president to retire due to succession dispute.
newsitem.headline: Avon president to retire due to succession dispute.

text.p: Avon Products Inc, the diversified cosmetics company, said Tuesday its president and chief operating officer Edward Robinson will retire June 1.
It said Robinson, 57, decided to leave due to a disagreement over the issue of management succession at the company.
Brian Martin, an Avon spokesman, said Robinson had disagreed with the board's decision to ask James Preston, Avon chairman and chief executive officer, to stay on for two more years.
Preston, 64, said in a company statement that he will remain at Avon for at least the next two years.
Avon said it had no immediate plans to name a successor to Robinson. It said his duties would be assumed by Preston.
Martin said Preston will add the title of president.

While there are no immediate candidates for the presidency, Avon has "a very strong group of senior operating officers, some of whom recently took on added responsibilities" in the company, Martin said.
Robinson joined Avon in 1989 as chief financial officer. He became president in 1993.
